targets.text: Culture Nodes accounts for every attempt and orchestrates humans, loops, and itself: failed attempts carry actor attribution and usage; evidence bindings resolve real run evidence and bridge-measured diffs; nodes pre-announce success criteria that are mechanically checked; humans execute nodes through the same lifecycle as agents; ad-hoc runs are first-class; and the system proves it live with a PR-upkeep flow sweeping Qodo and SonarCloud findings on this repo
The announcement holds only if every one of the eight issue surfaces ships with its live proof — a partial batch renders as partial delivery, never as the announced whole

Issue 40: thread actor attribution into worker failure completions — failAttempt/completeTechnicalFailure (internal/worker/worker.go:474,491) build CompletionRequest without ActorID across 26 failure sites; the resolved actorRowID (dispatch.go:92) is already a parameter at completeFromResult/park and in scope at the rest; DispatchContext (seams.go:49) is the natural carrier; code-path failures stamp codeRunnerActorID as their success paths already do (code.go:314); no migration needed, attempts.actor_id exists since 0002

After the fix, a forced dispatch failure of an agent node persists an attempt row whose actor_id is the resolved actor, and actor stats retry burn counts it; failure sites that fire before any actor resolution stay honestly NULL rather than guessing an actor

Issue 32 async: add optional usage to FailedPayload (internal/actors/protocol.go:250) and set req.Usage in the EventFailed branch of completionFor (internal/actors/callback.go:692-703); all three bridges emit usage on their non-domain failure branches only when a terminal result object exists — codex/claude/colleague CLIs already parse usage on error and incomplete results — keeping result-is-None crash and timeout branches usage-less per the migration-0012 no-fabricated-zero stance; all-backends rule applies

A failed async attempt whose bridge held a parseable terminal result persists that result's real token counts; a crash or timeout with no result object still persists NULL usage — zeros are never fabricated (migration 0012 stance); all three backends emit it, per the all-backends rule

Issue 32 sync: the sync failure path has the same NULL-usage hole — a bridge 500 body carries error, class, workspace_measured but no usage, and completeFromInvocationError (internal/worker/dispatch.go:300-316) discards it; honesty condition h24 (every attempt counted) needs the sync hole covered or explicitly narrowed

Either the sync failure path carries usage end-to-end (bridge 500 body plus completeFromInvocationError persisting it) or the h24 narrowing is restated explicitly in the delivery docs — silence about the sync hole is not an option

Issue 34: fix EvidenceForSubject empty-subject — projection.go:353 gates the whole loop on ref not empty while projectionKindFor (internal/worker/bindings.go:202) always passes empty for the evidence binding; make empty subject mean all live evidence for the run per examples/independent-review/README.md:135-144; reconcile the contradictory doc comments (projection.go:353-355 vs bindings.go:186-190); add the missing empty-subject subtest (projection_test.go:207) and make the bindings_test Projection stub project over real records (bindings_test.go:18-37)

An e2e test proves the delivery-loop verify node's testEvidence binding resolves the run's actually-appended evidence records — not merely that the projection function returns non-empty in a unit fixture

Issue 33a: give workspace_measured a landing surface — InvocationResult, CompletedPayload and FailedPayload (protocol.go:124,238,250) all silently drop it today while every bridge attaches it on every sync and terminal branch (the bridge workspace.py measures via git the bridge itself ran); the independent-review README recommends folding it into the `/nodes/<id>/output` answer since agent nodes cannot hold observe authority; web UI already anticipates a diffstat on evidence (web/src/domain/evidence.ts:13-25)

workspace_measured round-trips bridge to protocol to persisted node output on all three backends, stays actor-reported in authority terms (never observed), and a downstream node can bind it; the unmeasured case renders as unmeasured, never as an empty diff

Issue 33b: resolve the `/nodes/<id>/evidence` binding — the compiler accepts it (internal/compiler/contract.go:14-31) but the worker refuses at bindings.go:133-137 and the engine at binding.go:45; the fix needs node-run-scoped evidence selection and flips the TestUnresolvableBindingsFailLoudly assertion (bindings_test.go:127)

A downstream node binding `/nodes/<id>/evidence` receives exactly that node's evidence records, and the compile-clean-but-fail-at-dispatch trap closes: compiler-accepted binding surfaces and resolver-supported surfaces agree by test

Issue 39: implement the durable wait surface — a production WaitDispatcher (internal/worker/seams.go:159), the wait timer effect, and an inbound signal delivery route, so a flow can park on an external non-human event (Slack, Discord, Culture message per the issue) and resume; duration and timestamp waits fail at dispatch today too

A wait node parks its run durably (no lease held), resumes on an authenticated inbound signal or timer fire, and loop bounds still apply across the resume; an undelivered signal leaves the run parked and inspectable, never wedged

Issue 38a: humans as actors through the existing section-13 path — actors.kind is free text with no CHECK (migrations/0001:39-55), dispatch never reads kind (internal/worker/registry.go:93-128), and internal/actors/doc.go:6-20 names a human group as an intended case; a kind=human actor behind a human-inbox bridge speaking 202+callback needs zero new dispatch machinery
A kind=human actor completes a node through the standard 202-plus-callback path with zero actor-kind branching added to dispatch — the neutrality test stays green unmodified

Issue 38b: human task lifecycle and inbox — human_tasks are binary pending-to-decided today (internal/engine/types.go:241-248) with no claimed/in-progress/submitted states; the web UI has no approvals, review, grade, or human-task surface at all (web/src/api/client.ts exposes exactly two POSTs: workflow validate and publish) though the visual vocabulary exists (AuthorityChip, waiting glyph, human glyph family in mesh.ts:36-58); actor registration is only deploy/prod/register-actor.sh hardcoding kind=agent — no HTTP registration endpoint (internal/api/actors.go:49-53)

A human can list their pending tasks and submit a result from the web UI without shell access, and actor registration happens through an authenticated API rather than raw SQL on the production database

Issue 37: pre-announced success criteria — acceptance.requires exists per node in the schema (workflow.schema.json nodeAcceptance) with a 9-kind vocabulary but only process_exit and workspace_diff are evaluable (internal/runners/acceptance.go:72-81), wired post-hoc on the code-node success path only and never affecting routing (internal/worker/acceptance.go:29-33); the success_signal ledger record type is fully specified with a mechanical flag and has zero evaluators; no workflow-level acceptance block exists

A node whose pre-announced acceptance check fails routes per its declared policy — as contract_rejected or a declared domain outcome, never by inventing an undeclared outcome — and the evaluation appends derived-authority records; mechanical success_signal records get evaluated, non-mechanical ones honestly stay unevaluated

Issue 36: first-class ad-hoc runs — runs require a published digest today (internal/api/runs.go:44), the nodes run CLI verb is a stub (cmd/nodes/modes.go:18-29), and the nodes-operator skill's assign verb already proves the ergonomics by rendering a one-node workflow, publishing, creating, and polling in bash; promote that shape into the API and CLI
One command or API call runs an ad-hoc instruction, and the resulting run is a normal pinned-digest run — ad-hoc never bypasses publish semantics, digest pinning, or the ledger

Live test: a PR-upkeep flow ships as the dogfood workflow — sweep sources are open PRs' Qodo findings plus SonarCloud unresolved issues for agentculture_culture-nodes (today: zero open PRs; four unresolved code smells — BLOCKER python:S3516 culture_nodes/cli/_commands/node_runs.py:42, two CRITICAL go:S3776 in tests/deploy, one MINOR godre:S8193) — and the flow loops: pick item, fix or propose, review, human gate, next

The PR-upkeep flow completes at least one live run against real Sonar or Qodo items with an externally-driven trigger, produces at least one fix that passes a human gate before merge, and renders failed or empty sweeps honestly instead of claiming success

Provider neutrality is test-enforced — internal/actors/neutrality_test.go greps actors, worker, engine, compiler, api — so human-actor work must not introduce actor-kind branching in dispatch; the grades API (internal/api/grades.go:26-45) stays the one sanctioned kind-aware spot
internal/actors/neutrality_test.go remains unmodified and green through the whole batch; any new kind-aware code lives outside dispatch, following the grades-API precedent

The ledger authority ladder is untouched: agents propose, runner-boundary code observes, validators derive, humans confirm only via CommitReview — acceptance and KPI evaluation land as derived records, and bridge-measured workspace facts remain actor-reported rather than observed unless routed through the runner boundary (the fold-into-output recommendation honors this)
No code path added in this batch writes observed-authority evidence from an agent path or promotes a proposal without a human; CommitReview stays the only writer of confirmed authority

Operators of the culture-nodes control plane (Ori and mesh operators with the nodes-operator skill), workflow authors, the registered actor fleet (claude-code bridge on spark, codex-thor, codex-orin, future human actors), and the per-actor analytics consumers of issue 28

Each named audience gets at least one shipped surface in this batch: operators get ad-hoc runs and the upkeep flow, workflow authors get working evidence bindings and routable acceptance, the actor fleet gets attribution and usage on failure, analytics gets true retry burn

After shipping: every attempt — failed included — carries actor attribution, and usage wherever a terminal result existed; verify nodes receive the run's real evidence and the builder's bridge-measured diff; a flow can park on an external signal or a human and resume; humans execute nodes through the same actor protocol as agents; success criteria are declared before a node runs and route the flow when unmet; one command runs an ad-hoc instruction; and a live PR-upkeep loop sweeps Qodo and SonarCloud findings on this repo through the system itself
Every clause of the after-state maps to at least one confirmed requirement and one c24 success signal — no aspirational clause ships without a claim behind it

Today: failed worker-path attempts persist NULL actor_id (undercounting exactly the retry burn that defines per-actor cost), failed async attempts persist NULL usage even when the bridge had real token counts, the evidence projection binding resolves empty so both shipped loop examples review blind, bridge-measured workspace facts are dropped on every path, humans are binary approve/reject gates outside the actor lifecycle, acceptance checks are post-hoc and toothless, ad-hoc work needs a hand-rendered workflow in bash, and repo upkeep happens in operator sessions, not through the product
Every before-state deficiency is reproducible today at the file:line its scope entry cites — the description comes from read code, not recollection

The product's brand line is 'every node has a contract, every result has evidence' — and the gaps cluster exactly where honesty is hardest: failures, reviews, and humans. Unattributed failed attempts misstate the retry-burn signal issue 28's analytics need; blind verify nodes make independent review a fiction; and until the system can run its own upkeep, dogfooding stays aspirational

The two central harms are demonstrable on live data: the 2026-08-13 codex-orin failed run persists an unattributed usage-less attempt, and the loop examples' testEvidence binding resolves empty against a run with appended evidence

Mechanically checkable: (1) GET /v1alpha1/actors/{id}/stats counts a forced failed agent attempt in retry burn with non-NULL actor_id; (2) delivery-loop's verify node receives non-empty testEvidence in e2e; (3) all three bridges round-trip usage on a failed attempt with a terminal result and workspace_measured into bound node output; (4) a wait-node flow parks and resumes on a delivered signal; (5) a kind=human actor completes a node through the callback path with neutrality tests green; (6) an acceptance-failing node routes its declared outcome; (7) one CLI/API call runs an ad-hoc instruction; (8) the PR-upkeep flow completes a live run on real Sonar/Qodo items producing at least one human-gated merged fix
Each of the eight signals is mechanically checked at delivery time; any signal that cannot actually be run then is demoted to an explicit follow-up rather than quietly claimed
The PR-upkeep flow supports only the culture-nodes repo for now; sweeping other repos is out of scope until a follow-up extends it

The shipped upkeep workflow names culture-nodes as its only sweep target (hard-coded or single-value input); multi-repo support exists nowhere in the delivered code and is a recorded follow-up, not an undocumented capability

Challenge/security: every mutating surface this batch adds — inbound signal delivery, actor registration, human task submission from the web — ships authenticated from day one, extending the decision endpoint's bearer-token pattern (requireDecisionAuth, internal/api/humantasks.go:94-123, today's ONLY authenticated mutating route); the phase-1 authless-by-design posture does not extend to routes that can redirect dispatch to arbitrary endpoints or complete attempts
At delivery, no route added by this batch that mutates state accepts an unauthenticated request — verified by handler tests; the authless surfaces remain read-only

Challenge/lifecycle: human-actor attempts need human-timescale deadlines — async attempts carry a wait-bound deadline timer and a dispatch budget of 3 per work item (engine hardening, issues 16/19), which would time out and retry a human taking days; the human-node authoring pattern must set explicit long deadlines per node (authorable config, not actor-kind branching, preserving neutrality) and the budget/park interplay must be verified for human resubmission
A human-actor node authored with a long deadline parks for days without timeout, retry, or budget exhaustion — proven by a time-manipulated test; no engine code branches on actor kind to achieve it

Challenge/cost-containment: routable acceptance (c13) must compose with retry deliberately — an acceptance failure routed as contract_rejected re-enters failOrRetry (internal/engine/complete.go:382) and can automatically re-burn billable sessions; the declared enforce policy states whether retry applies, and the dispatch budget stays the backstop
For each enforce policy the routing-versus-retry behavior is declared and tested; no acceptance failure silently triggers unbounded paid retries
